name: Panhispanism
summary: Panhispanism promotes social, economic and cultural cooperation among Spain and the Spanish-speaking countries, with political unification as a goal for some. Its classic form, Hispanidad as defended by Ramiro de Maeztu, grounds the community in the Spanish language, Catholicism and a shared imperial history, and sets duty and hierarchy against liberalism and democracy. It is typically hostile to US influence and to the Black Legend about Spain.
scope: The mainstream Hispanidad strand: Maeztu's Defensa de la Hispanidad (1934), Acción Española and its Francoist continuation, plus the language-centred cultural integrationism of Menéndez Pidal and Ortiz and the anti-US, integration-minded present-day revival (for example the Parlamento Global Hispano, 2022). Left-wing Latin American unity projects in the Bolívar tradition are not the basis; many economic and social questions are not addressed by the doctrine, so those answers are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Ramiro de Maeztu
keyFigures.role: Author of Defensa de la Hispanidad and co-founder of Acción Española.

keyFigures.name: Ramón Menéndez Pidal
keyFigures.role: Philologist who promoted a unified Spanish language across the Hispanic world.

keyFigures.name: Fernando Ortiz
keyFigures.role: Cuban writer who framed panhispanism as integration opposed to US-led pan-Americanism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Panhispanism has no health program; Catholic social teaching and corporatist paternalism lean toward state care, but Falangist and liberal strands of the movement split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Never addressed; corporatist and Social Catholic strands favour a just wage, but the movement spans left and right, so adherents are split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Maeztu criticised the cult of wealth and US finance and sought harmony between capital and labour, so unrestrained markets are not a Hispanic ideal.

public-ownership.rationale: Not a stated theme; corporatist Hispanism prefers guilds and organic bodies over nationalised industry, though Falangists accepted some state control.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No documented stance; Social Catholic duty of the rich is balanced by conservative property views, so adherents split.

unions-good.rationale: Hispanists favoured guild-type bodies bringing workers and employers together rather than independent unions, so the answer is mixed.

property-fundamental.rationale: Maeztu defended private property against the revolutionary abolition of it, while tying it to social function.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Maeztu attacked US bankers acting as co-legislators over Hispanic states, but there is no general program on corporate regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from Social Catholic and paternalist corporatism, which values care for the poor; not documented for the movement as such.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Maeztu admired guild hierarchy of apprentices, journeymen and masters, not collective worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian, order-first outlook of Acción Española and the Francoist form of Hispanidad.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic-conservative moral outlook of Hispanidad; no explicit treatment.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Never addressed; authoritarian strands favour censorship, but modern Hispanists cite free speech against the Black Legend.

strong-leader.rationale: Acción Española wanted an authoritarian monarchy and Francoist Hispanidad was bound up with a dictator, though Maeztu stressed duty and hierarchy rather than personal rule.

state-harmful.rationale: Maeztu defended organic hierarchy, nation and authority and attacked both anarchic liberty and the omnipotent state, so the idea that the state is unnecessary is alien.

empower-police-military.rationale: Acción Española relied on the army as guarantor of order, and Francoist Hispanidad was military-backed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic moral framework; not discussed in the sources.

decide-locally.rationale: The movement stresses unity of the Hispanic world and the nation, though Maeztu's organic society values local bodies; slight lean against devolving everything.

rehabilitation.rationale: No documented position; Catholic tradition supports both reform and retribution.

traditional-family.rationale: Catholic family order is part of the Hispanic ethos as described by Maeztu and the Francoist Hispanidad.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Hispanidad tradition is explicitly Catholic and traditionalist, which opposes it; Francoist Spain was a confessional state.

abortion-legal.rationale: Core Catholic position within the Hispanidad tradition; Spain's Catholic identity is central to Maeztu.

more-religion-public.rationale: Maeztu defines Hispanidad as a spiritual community united by language and Catholicism, with the faith central to public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Hispanidad presents itself as already race-transcending through mestizaje, so special remedies are seen as unnecessary; modern strands may differ.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from traditional Catholic anthropology; the sources do not discuss gender theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Maeztu called for a return to pure Spanishness and the movement centres on preserving Hispanic culture and language.

gradual-change.rationale: Maeztu defended tradition and the harmony of tradition and progress and attacked revolutionary borrón y cuenta nueva.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Hispanists welcome Hispanic immigrants as kin while Spanish traditionalists oppose other immigration; no uniform position.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Panhispanism seeks regional Hispanic bodies and opposes US-led pan-Americanism rather than global governance.

free-trade.rationale: Hispanic integration favours internal trade within the bloc, but anti-US economic sentiment resists open markets; split.

nation-first.rationale: The movement is both nationalist about Spain or the Hispanic community and internationalist among Hispanic states, so the framing does not fit cleanly.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The sources record no Hispanist view on rights-based force, and anti-US sentiment and Catholic just-war thinking pull in opposite directions.

open-borders.rationale: Free movement within the Hispanic world is favoured by some, but open borders in general are not part of the doctrine.

limit-growth.rationale: Not an environmental ideology; Maeztu opposed materialism but did not call for limiting growth.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Maeztu distrusted materialist modern civilisation and emphasised spiritual values, so faith in technology is weak.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy lies outside the doctrine, and the sources give adherents no common line on it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Maeztu condemned revolutionary slogans and the French Revolution, though Bolivar-era unity projects arose from independence wars.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from elitist, hierarchical, anti-democratic organic thinking.

central-planning.rationale: Not a Hispanist theme; corporatism prefers organic bodies to a planned command economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: The doctrine does not discuss market socialism, and corporatists and liberals within the movement would answer differently.

land-value-tax.rationale: No Hispanist source treats single-tax proposals, so there is no basis for a lean.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from conservative defence of family property and hierarchies of blood.

basic-income.rationale: Basic income is a modern policy the movement has not discussed, and Social Catholic and conservative strands would split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Anti-US economic nationalism and self-sufficient Hispanic integration lean toward protection.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Falangist and corporatist strands accept state direction; others do not.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Social Catholic distributism links to Maeztu's later thought, favouring wide distribution of property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred: Maeztu defended guild hierarchy and property, which excludes abolishing wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not discussed; Maeztu complained of foreign bankers dictating to Hispanic states, but proposed no abolition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Acción Española envisioned a corporatist monarchy and Maeztu admired the guild system with its graded hierarchy.

one-party-rule.rationale: Francoist Hispanidad coexisted with single-party rule, but Maeztu's model was a monarchy of corporate bodies, and modern Hispanism is pluralist.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Maeztu belonged to the monarchist Acción Española and described the Spanish empire as a missionary Monarquía Católica.

democracy-best.rationale: Maeztu argued that rationalism and democracy are foreign to the Hispanic ethos and wrote that democracy ends by ruining the state through spoils.

direct-votes.rationale: Following Maeztu's rejection of democracy, plebiscitary politics is disfavoured; modern strands would be less hostile.

workers-councils.rationale: Alien to the corporatist, hierarchical and anti-revolutionary Hispanist tradition.

right-to-secede.rationale: Panhispanism seeks unity, and Spanish nationalist Hispanists oppose secession such as in Catalonia.

natural-rulers.rationale: Maeztu spoke of natural and blood aristocracies as the bulwark of societies and defended hierarchy against levelling.

political-violence-never.rationale: Maeztu's circle plotted a coup and Francoism rose by civil war, though the cultural movement itself is not violent.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred from the militant, missionary self-image of imperial Spain in Maeztu's account.

separate-church-state.rationale: Maeztu's account ties Spain's identity to Catholicism and the Francoist Hispanidad equated the nation with the faith, rejecting separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Catholic natural law and tradition guide Hispanist thought, not scripture-based law as such, so a split answer.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Contrary to the organic state and authority emphasised by Hispanist writers.

military-superiority.rationale: Francoist imperial rhetoric was expansive; modern Hispanism is cultural, not military.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Hispanidad is defined by language, faith and mestizaje rather than by a single ethnic group.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Maeztu rejects class warfare and seeks harmony between capital and labour and between nation and hierarchies.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Maeztu affirms essential equality of souls but defends differences of position and hierarchy.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Hispanidad celebrates the mixed legacy of the conquest; indigenous authority is not part of it and indigenism is typically opposed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Hispanists defend the Spanish empire against the Black Legend and Maeztu vindicates the colonisation.

civilizational-union.rationale: Panhispanism is defined as cooperation among Hispanic countries with political unification as a goal, built on shared language, history and Catholicism.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Maeztu advocates duty over rights and criticised the cult of wealth.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Maeztu's motto of duty, hierarchy and humanity explicitly replaces liberty, equality and fraternity.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is outside the movement's concerns; Catholic creation theology gives mixed signals.

limit-population.rationale: Catholic and Francoist pronatalism opposes population control.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Maeztu criticised materialist modernity but did not reject industrial society.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The tradition values continuity over disruption.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from human hierarchy and moral authority emphasis.

restore-past-order.rationale: Maeztu called for a return to pure Spanishness and Acción Española spoke of restoring the values of La Raza.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Hispanism is doctrine-driven, grounded in tradition and faith.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred from preference for institutions, hierarchy and the army; though some strands engaged in conspiracy.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources say nothing on prefigurative method, so adherents are not united.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contrary to the civilising claim of Hispanic heritage.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Guild hierarchy of apprentices, officers and masters assumes a division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Charity is a Catholic duty but a need-based communist principle conflicts with Maeztu's anti-communism.

production-for-use.rationale: A socialist slogan not engaged by Hispanist writers, who accept profit under social duty.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Maeztu rejected the Marxist reading of capital and labour as opposed classes.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Maeztu denounces the Soviet regime and revolutionary class politics as despotic.

collective-farming.rationale: Contrary to property defence and anti-communism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Maeztu blamed US financial power for Hispanic ills but the Marxist thesis is not Hispanist doctrine.

taxation-theft.rationale: Contrary to the duty-based organic state.

harm-principle.rationale: Hispanidad rejects liberal individualism; morals and order justify restriction.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Maeztu replaced liberal rights language with duty and hierarchy and viewed society as organic.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from state, army and duty emphasis.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Opposes market-style view of the state.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred; Maeztu criticised cult of wealth and treats the state as a moral order.

positive-liberty.rationale: Hispanist thinkers dismiss liberal freedom talk generally and offer no stand on material conditions of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Traditionalist critics often claim cultural elites dominate; mild inference from the Black Legend discourse.

organic-representation.rationale: Acción Española envisioned a corporatist Cortes representing bodies, and Maeztu favoured the guild system.

total-state.rationale: Maeztu condemned omnipotent states as despotic, though Francoism was highly statist.

national-rebirth.rationale: Maeztu urged a return to pure Spanishness and Acción Española wanted to revive La Raza values that Spain had abandoned.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Francoist Hispanidad had imperial rhetoric, later softened to cultural influence; modern Hispanism seeks voluntary integration.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Maeztu's ideal was a hierarchy of duty within a national Catholic monarchy, not feudal personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Contrary to the humanist claim of essential equality in Maeztu.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Hispanist Catholic thought upholds objective truth and the good.

universal-morality.rationale: Maeztu's Hispanic humanism rests on universal Christian truths of the soul's essential equality.

single-common-good.rationale: Organic and Catholic thinking aims at a common good and harmony of parts rather than interest balancing.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; Acción Española was antisemitic but modern Hispanists vary.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Hispanic nationality laws offer privileges to descendants and Hispanic peoples, a mild inference.

revive-national-language.rationale: Panhispanism promotes Spanish as a shared language rather than reviving lost ones, though a Philippine group promotes it.

school-vouchers.rationale: Catholic school freedom is an inferred preference.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal doctrine is outside the movement's concerns and adherents hold varied economic views.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not addressed; split between liberal and corporatist Hispanists.

rule-by-example.rationale: Maeztu stressed duty and moral hierarchy, inferring leadership by moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Hispanic independence is celebrated, but Hispanists also seek to dissolve borders in a wider community.

force-without-un.rationale: The movement is cultural and opposes US unilateralism, but no source gives a rule on UN approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Maeztu denounces rationalism as foreign to the Hispanic ethos and grounds Hispanidad in faith.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Hispanists treat Hispanic migrants as kin and others as outsiders, so no single line emerges.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The sources are silent on workfare, and Catholic charity and conservative work ethic pull apart.

class-collaboration.rationale: Maeztu seeks harmony of capital and labour and the guild system rather than class opposition.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The tradition prizes inherited culture and spiritual heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Panhispanism is described as opposed to the United States and Anglo-Saxon influence, seeking Hispanic unity against it.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred from Falangist and corporatist national organisation of workers, against Marxist internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Catholic traditionalism suggests distinct roles; a modest inference.

ban-interest.rationale: Catholic tradition once condemned usury, but Hispanists accept banking; mild disagreement.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Maeztu writes that Spaniards affirm the essential equality of all men whatever their race and Hispanidad is defined by mestizaje.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist view of the state contradicts the organic, hierarchical view.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production is not a doctrinal issue for the movement.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Language and culture unity matter, but Hispanic immigrants are kin, so mild agreement.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not part of the Hispanist doctrine, though some far-right adherents share it.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; anti-party corporatists dislike parties.

national-mission.rationale: Maeztu portrays the empire as a missionary monarchy carrying Catholic faith, giving a sense of mission.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Maeztu wrote that democracy ruins the state by distributing favours to voters.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Defence of the Francoist legacy and army role inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Contrary to the organic state and corporatism.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Hispanidad stresses mestizaje; Salvador de Madariaga and Julian Marias praised mixing and Maeztu's equality of souls.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Maeztu affirms the essential equality of all men's souls though not equality of position or legal status.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is an internal Marxist debate which Hispanist writers, who reject socialism outright, never entered.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Hispanists defend the colonisation and treat Spanish America as an extension of Spain.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Hispanist writers did not address religious personal law; Spain's own civil law is already uniform.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Catholic confessional state under Franco limited other religions, but not a Hispanist theme.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Contrary to Hispanic customs; beef is central in Hispanic culture and never raised.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Catholic education is central to Hispanidad.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The question presumes a socialist state, which Hispanism rejects, so it offers no answer.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Maeztu denied that sovereignty rests on a popular will, preferring the monarchic and traditional order.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist goals are not part of the doctrine; anti-US economics gives no specific trade rule.

population-transfer.rationale: Contrary to the inclusive Hispanic community ideal.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Maeztu opposed the idea in favour of harmony and cooperation.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Authoritarian strands favoured suppression of Marxist parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory is not engaged by Hispanist authors, who talk of duty and hierarchy.

separated-powers.rationale: Maeztu criticised power absolutised; a balance among principles but not Montesquieu per se.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Catholic social teaching suggests priority, an inference.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is outside the movement's concerns.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The community is mixed and diversity is a Hispanic hallmark, but cohesion by language and faith is valued.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: No Hispanist source treats price fixing, and corporatist and market strands would differ.

party-controls-media.rationale: Francoist censorship existed; modern Hispanism uses social media freely.

party-commands-army.rationale: Army was independent guardian in Acción Española vision.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Hispanic nationals benefit from shorter waits under Spanish law, so Hispanists favour fast-track for kin.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Hierarchical organic thought has no egalitarian pay rule for officials, so a mild disagreement is inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party organisation is not a Hispanist theme, and anti-party corporatists and Falangists differ in practice.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Panhispanism seeks social, economic and political cooperation or unification among Hispanic states, as with the Parlamento Global Hispano created in 2022.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Hispanidad is Catholic, an episcopal church; Primate Goma equated Hispanidad with Catholicism.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Catholic tradition holds church influence but not theocracy; Maeztu was a layman and monarchist.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential term limits do not feature in Hispanist writing, which favours monarchy or strong rulers over elections.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anti-US stance suggests but Spain is in NATO; split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Mandatory universal ownership is a utopian scheme alien to Hispanist thought, which defends ordinary property relations.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Traditionalists romanticise rural Hispanic life; inference.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Panhispanism treats the Hispanic world as one divided community to be unified.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist anti-intellectualism is not part of Hispanism, which includes academy figures like Menendez Pidal.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Hispanists defend Hispanic civilisation as superior, as in Maeztu, though essential human equality is affirmed.

death-penalty.rationale: Francoist and conservative Catholic strands accepted it, though the Church cautions.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic moral education that Hispanidad associates with Spanish identity.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic teaching accepts evolution.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic moral conservatism of the Hispanidad tradition and Francoist censorship.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Hispanist community privileges descendants and Spanish-language peoples.

minority-language-support.rationale: Unity around Spanish as the common language, per Menendez Pidal's emphasis.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Minority exemptions are not discussed, and a Catholic-identified movement has no clear line on them.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Hispanic anti-US sentiment resents US banker influence over loans, as Maeztu noted.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Maeztu criticised dependence on foreign finance, implying economic autonomy.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is not addressed; Maeztu preferred tradition to rewriting by assemblies.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Charity duty plus Hispanic solidarity inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear strategy is outside the movement's concerns.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the monarchist preference of Acción Española for a non-elected head of state.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Anti-banker sentiment and national sovereignty over finance.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial bargaining is not discussed, and the movement seeks unity by cooperation rather than land claims.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Social Catholic doctrine on social function of property in Maeztu's later distributism.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; Maeztu denounced Soviet system as despotic but not in these terms.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is outside the doctrine and the sources give no signal.

collective-defense.rationale: Hispanic solidarity would treat attack on one as attack on all; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: International law on annexation is not discussed in the sources; Hispanists criticised the US territorial expansion after 1848 but give no rule.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Maeztu and Francoist Hispanidad defended a Catholic Church with a leading role and not subordinated.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Spanish unionist Hispanists would agree; others not.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special-autonomy arrangements are not addressed, and unionist Spanish Hispanists would doubt them while integrationists welcome autonomy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Catholic sacral monarchy, but not divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not a doctrinal matter for Hispanists.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nature-versus-nurture is not addressed, though the Catholic view of the soul stresses essential equality.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Maeztu condemned arbitrary authority among the destructive absolutes.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not part of the doctrine.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Maeztu stressed harmony of principles such as authority and liberty, nation and hierarchies.

leader-cult.rationale: Francoist cult existed; Hispanist cultural strands do not require it.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody rules are not addressed by the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The question concerns Maoist theory and has no counterpart in Hispanist thought.

refugee-return.rationale: Not part of the movement's themes, so no line is documented.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not a feature; unity among Hispanic states is sought through cooperation.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Confessional-state strands favoured it; mainstream modern rejects.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not part of Catholic Hispanic custom.

common-currency.rationale: Economic integration among Hispanic countries is a stated aim of the Parlamento Global Hispano; a common currency follows.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Panhispanism holds that peoples sharing the Spanish language and ancestry should integrate politically, as Bolivar and later movements wished.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Hispanism emphasises a common language and culture rather than minority cultural self-government.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The question concerns diaspora minorities; Hispanism has no documented line.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Maeztu grounds history in spiritual and religious forces, not in economic base.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not addressed; corporatists accept trade bodies while others favour antitrust.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not a Hispanist theme, though Maeztu denounced bankers' influence over states.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Constitutional review is not discussed; the movement rejects liberal democracy but also majoritarian populism.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from the traditional Catholic view of gender roles that the Hispanidad tradition upholds.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Hispanic bloc integration is sought but autarky in the Francoist sense is not a modern aim.

moral-incentives.rationale: Maeztu praised duty, but Hispanists accept wages and wealth, so there is no line on replacing material incentives.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Maeztu praises natural aristocracies of blood and the hierarchies as the bulwark of society.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Hispanists fight the Black Legend and promote Hispanic history, with Menendez Pidal on language and culture.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Maeztu vindicates the Spanish colonisation as a civilising Catholic mission.

patriotic-education.rationale: Pride in Hispanic heritage and nation is central to the movement.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: US-style affirmative action is not a Hispanist theme and the Hispanic world has no common line.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not discussed in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marxist crisis theory is not engaged, though Maeztu predicted continued decline of liberal capitalism.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Francoist Hispanidad created a Council of the Hispanidad to manage relations with Latin America and the movement promotes Spain's cultural ties to former colonies.

delink-world-market.rationale: Integration within Hispanic world not delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Leninist debate not taken up by Hispanists.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Hispanist doctrine stresses duty and community over liberal property absolutism, so mild disagreement is inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism viewed as foreign by Maeztu.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Hispanists do not address colonial boundary treaties, which is outside their concerns.

elective-rulers.rationale: Monarchist Acción Española rejected elective rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Contrary to hierarchical order and authority.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Spanish Catholic tradition accepts resistance to tyrants; inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not part of the doctrine, and Hispanic traditions such as bullfighting divide adherents.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Maeztu's duty and hierarchy motto implies obligations of the higher toward the lower.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is activist and calls for national revival.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt School critique of media is not part of Hispanism, though Maeztu criticised materialist modernity.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is not addressed.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Panhispanism opposes US economic dominance, Maeztu criticising financial control over Hispanic states.

native-born-offices.rationale: Hispanic nationals often share rights across Hispanic states, so adherents lack one line.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist party relations are not applicable to Hispanism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not documented, though economic integration among Hispanic states is stressed.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Hispanists do not make territorial revanchist demands against neighbours as a doctrine.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenism is generally rejected by Hispanists, who defend a mestizo community.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Hispanidad ideology emerged within Falangist and Francoist contexts hostile to antifascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Hispanists condemn communism but not fascism equally.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: US history debate not addressed, though Hispanists are hostile to the US generally.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Defenders of the imperial legacy oppose removing monuments; modern movement defends Spain against the Black Legend.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-policy debates of this kind are not addressed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Maeztu argues democracy, liberalism and rationalism are foreign to the Hispanic ethos, which needs its own institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Acción Española built cells in the army and Francoism relied on it as guardian.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages for housework is not discussed, though Catholic family emphasis would give care work moral esteem.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Anti-US economic sentiment suggests defending strategic firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Catholic marriage doctrine and Francoist law banned divorce.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not a doctrinal matter.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Community ownership of land contradicts the defence of private property attributed to Maeztu.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Fiscal constitution is not discussed; Acción Española proposed a corporatist Cortes but its budget powers are not documented.

single-official-language.rationale: Menendez Pidal promoted a unified Spanish language as bond of the community.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The movement welcomes Hispanic investment, while its anti-US tendency would resist US purchases; no line.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Hispanidad claims to transcend race and favours equal treatment without outcome-based remedies, which is inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Maeztu criticised the fascination with wealth and the materialist civilisation.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert-war policy is not a doctrinal matter.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Bloc-enforcement of order is not discussed, though Hispanists criticised US interventions.

corporate-influence.rationale: Maeztu criticised bankers acting as co-legislators.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from anti-US sentiment and suspicion of foreign financial influence in Hispanic countries.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property restrictions are not addressed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Public-employment guarantees are not discussed, though Falangist strands stressed a right to work.

non-intervention.rationale: Hispanic nations historically opposed US intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union form is not discussed; the corporatist tradition favours mixed guild-like bodies.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Acción Española adopted an antisemitic discourse, but mainstream Hispanism does not.

local-production.rationale: Localism is not a Hispanist theme, since the movement seeks a larger integrated economy.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Sovereignty versus international law is not addressed; Hispanists want supranational Hispanic bodies but not a global order.

religious-nation.rationale: Maeztu and Primate Goma equated Hispanidad with Catholicism, though it can be cultural.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Panhispanism is described as anti-American and opposed to Anglo-Saxon influence, so tributary deference to a leading power is rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on unity and solidarity across regions of Spain and the Hispanic community.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: Maeztu opposed abolishing private property and communism.

defeat-communism.rationale: Maeztu denounced the Soviet regime and the movement is anti-communist.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery models are not discussed.

religion-illusion.rationale: Maeztu grounds Hispanidad on Catholic faith as the substance of the community.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Hispanist writers criticise materialism and do not accept the Marxist developmental story, so no clear line.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from traditional Catholic gender views and rejection of Marxist economic determinism.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic emphasis on the family as the proper place of child and home care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; the Real Academia promotes a unified Spanish.

treaties-binding.rationale: Indigenous treaty questions are not addressed.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small commune-based society is alien to the nation-wide, imperial and hierarchical vision.

majority-settlement.rationale: Ethnic settlement policy is not part of Hispanidad, which emphasises mixing and shared faith, so mild disagreement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Maeztu opposed Soviet communism and criticised US financial capitalism, favouring a Catholic third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical or sacred land claims are not part of the doctrine's documented content.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not part of the doctrine, though extreme-right adherents may.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Francoist law did, modern Catholic Hispanists less so.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Francoist Hispanidad coexisted with repression, while the modern cultural movement is not documented as favouring it.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Confessional-state strands within Hispanidad supported penalties for offences against the Catholic faith.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Hispanists describe the empire as missionary, not exploitative.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: This is an Islamic doctrine foreign to Hispanism, which in its tradition defines itself as Catholic.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not a Hispanist tenet; Catholic tradition does not endorse removing rulers for lacking religious law, though Spanish Carlists saw legitimacy that way.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Maeztu criticised democracy and mass participation as ruinous, so broad direct participation is disfavoured.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Contrary to the harmony of classes.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Contrary to Catholic anthropology and traditional gender views of the Hispanidad tradition.

assisted-dying.rationale: Catholic doctrine opposes it and the Hispanidad tradition is Catholic.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Maeztu offered a third course against both liberalism and socialism, though the movement still sits on the right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist concept opposed by Maeztu's guild and class-harmony view.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Reconquista tradition may suggest it, but not a core doctrine.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Catholic monarchy and Hispanidad rooted in faith, with authority from God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic public presence favoured by Hispanidad.

social-market-economy.rationale: The movement does not specify an economic model, and German-style ordoliberalism is not a Hispanist theme.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Acción Española treated the army as guardian of order, and Francoist Hispanidad relied on it.

rich-first.rationale: Gradualist development theory is not addressed.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Anti-US and anti-Soviet, as per Maeztu's naming of two rival powers.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Acción Española sought a Catholic monarchy, which by nature passes the crown within a dynasty.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual banking is not discussed, though Maeztu criticised international bankers.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Maeztu noted bankers imposed fiscal reforms on Hispanic republics.

property-franchise.rationale: Suffrage qualifications are not discussed in the sources, though democracy itself is rejected.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is alien to the traditional Catholic Hispanist outlook.

reification.rationale: Marxist theory of commodity form is not engaged by Hispanists.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Maeztu criticised the power of money but did not make this press argument.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule of law ideal in tradition.

racial-franchise.rationale: Hispanidad as described transcends racial categories and Maeztu affirms the equality of all men regardless of race.

online-participation.rationale: Digital democracy is not addressed, although the modern movement thrives on social media.

open-government-data.rationale: Transparency tools are not part of the doctrine.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic canon law restricts, but civil restriction is not a Hispanist demand.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Hispanidad as described transcends race and treats the Hispanic community as inclusive, though Acción Española had antisemitic strands.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Random assemblies conflict with hierarchy and natural aristocracy.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist Catholic emphasis on fidelity to inherited doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Hispanists criticise the fascination of wealth but frame it as a moral issue, not liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist outlook and army-as-guardian view.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Maeztu bases the community on Catholicism so state atheism is anathema.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Hispanist thought prizes order, authority and hierarchy, which abolitionism contradicts.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Maeztu rejects racial supremacies and affirms the essential equality of all people whatever their race, and Hispanidad is built on mixing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred: Catholic, corporatist Hispanism leans on the Church and organic communities for welfare, but the sources do not discuss it directly.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: Maeztu and Acción Española set hierarchy and duty against liberal democracy, so limits on rulers' tenure are not a theme.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine opposes liberal and democratic mass politics, so a delegated voting system runs against it.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine, which focuses on culture, language and community, and nothing in it points either way.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Catholic basis of Hispanidad, as Maeztu and the Francoist version describe it, keeps priesthood and church office for men.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Catholic family order in Hispanidad assigns the husband headship of the household, as in Francoist Spain.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: Hispanidad promotes a community of Hispanic peoples, favouring shared rights among them.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: corporatist and hierarchical Hispanism treats property as a function and is wary of state price-setting.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: Maeztu defends property and order against communism.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Francoist continuation of Hispanidad ran state youth organisations; inferred from that, not from the sources directly.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the anti-US stance of Panhispanism, though Francoist Spain itself hosted US bases.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the anti-US and sovereignty-minded stance, though Francoist Spain hosted US bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Hispanists defend the colonisation against the Black Legend, so formal recognition of conquest-era killings as genocide is resisted.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Maeztu ties property to social function and service, so reward follows work; inferred, as his stress is on duty and hierarchy.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from Catholic doctrine, which permits legitimate defence of self and others.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Hispanidad treats the community as continuous from Rome and the Catholic monarchy to the present.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic, traditionalist outlook of Maeztu and Accion Espanola.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic, traditionalist outlook of Hispanidad.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Francoist Hispanidad honoured the fallen and Catholic martyrs; inferred, as the sources do not detail it.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Maeztu frames Hispanidad as a Catholic mission against liberal and communist materialism.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Hispanidad treats Spain as the cultural and spiritual centre of the Hispanic world, not as a state gathering all its people.

culture-before-state.rationale: Integration begins with language and culture, with political union a goal only for some.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from Catholic traditionalism, which speaks of God as Father.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: Hispanidad is built on mestizaje and a community across races, not on one majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the aim of political unification of the Hispanic world for some adherents.

missingStatements.text: The Spanish colonisation of the Americas did more good than harm for the peoples colonised.
missingStatements.rationale: Maeztu vindicates the Spanish colonisation as a Catholic civilising mission and modern Hispanists defend Spain against the Black Legend.

missingStatements.text: A shared language is the strongest foundation for political cooperation between countries.
missingStatements.rationale: Menéndez Pidal promoted a unified Spanish language and Panhispanism builds integration on the shared language.

notes: Strands differ: the Francoist form was authoritarian and confessional, while the modern revival is a cultural and integrationist movement with looser economic views. Antisemitism appears in Acción Española but is not a mainstream tenet.
